name: Photo Contracts
description: Photography-specific commissions driven by collection records: capture unique subjects with required tags, meet a score threshold, and optionally require a pose. The component evaluates photographic evidence rather than generic kill, fetch, or reach objectives, so it complements progression.quest_log instead of encoding a parallel quest DSL. Contracts move from offered to active, ready, and completed; submission is explicit and completion is guarded once per profile and contract. It owns commission progress and claim state only. It does not score captures, store photographs, or pay rewards itself; completion events carry the configured reward payload for the owning economy or inventory system.

inputs.name: contracts
inputs.description: Definitions: id, required subject tags, minimum score, unique-subject target, optional pose tag, display text, prerequisites, and reward payload.

inputs.name: maxActiveContracts
inputs.description: Maximum simultaneously active commissions. New offers remain available without silently exceeding the player's tracking budget.

inputs.name: allowBestRecordEvidence
inputs.description: Whether an improved personal best can satisfy a commission after the subject's first recording. First-subject and best-score evidence remain distinct events either way.

outputs.name: contracts
outputs.description: Configured contracts with locked, offered, active, ready, or completed state and current unique-subject progress.

outputs.name: activeContracts
outputs.description: Active contract ids in acceptance order.

outputs.name: stateOf
outputs.description: stateOf(id): the contract state, or null for an unknown id.

provenance: Added 2026-10-29 with the Field Photography gameplay components (49ad258). Provenance written after the fact on 2026-10-29: it landed recording only "library-native". Nearest in a catalogue search: progression.quest_log and progression.level_objective_set; this judges photographic evidence and leaves generic objectives to the quest log rather than restating them. Library-native.
